questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Which countries grow the most coffee
Why coffee is bad for your health
How to make the perfect cup of coffee
Why the smell of coffee matters so much
questions.why: Neil says 'our topic today is the smell of coffee'.

questions.q: How much coffee does Catherine say she drinks?
options: One cup a day
A lot, about six cups a day
Only at weekends
Only two cups a week, at the weekend
questions.why: She jokes she drinks a cup 'every hour' and says she's had 'just the usual six cups'.

questions.q: What does Catherine say is the best thing about coffee?
options: The smell
The taste
The energy it gives her
The price
questions.why: Catherine says 'It's the smell. It's got to be the smell.'

questions.q: What do Neil and Catherine agree about coffee?
options: Take-away coffee always tastes better than coffee in a shop
It is too expensive
It never tastes as good as it smells
Big brands are the best
questions.why: Neil says it never tastes as good as it smells, and Catherine says 'Well no, not really.'

questions.q: According to coffee shop owner Tim Hayward, what happens when you smell coffee in a shop?
options: You feel sleepy
Your body reacts physically
You want to buy a different drink
You forget the taste
questions.why: He says when that smell hits you, 'you're getting physiological responses'.

questions.q: How does Catherine usually have her coffee?
options: She always drinks it in the shop
She makes it at home before she leaves for work
She drinks it from a glass
She usually takes it away in a paper cup
questions.why: She says she usually takes it away, in a tall paper cup with a lid.

questions.q: What does Tim Hayward find strange about large coffee chains?
options: Their cup lids stop you smelling the coffee
Their coffee is too hot to drink
They don't sell enough coffee
Their shops smell of food, not coffee
questions.why: He says the cups deliver the liquid past your tongue but stop any smell reaching your nose.

questions.q: Why does Neil ask Catherine about the lid on her cup?
options: Because plastic lids are bad for the environment
Because he wants to buy one
To make her think about the lid and the smell
Because her coffee keeps spilling
questions.why: Neil asks 'what is the effect of the lid on that experience?' since the smell is so important.
